result.verdict_on_request: Steps 19-20 are fixed. Step 42 is better but still does not fully answer Lee's note. Steps 19-20: the VCC/GND label sits about 40 css px clear of the parked wire's cap at 1440x628, and at all four sizes. V9, G9 and the display's pin stubs can be seen, with V9 and G9 most clearly at 1920. The step-list pictures are clean. Step 42: in the module's first two beats the wires now move as one piece with the board. The check finds no point where the USB cable passes through a wire, and on screen it lies in front of the wires it crosses. The A end's way can be followed at 760, 1000 and 1920: it stays below the caption box and on the canvas in all 21 frames. But four things a student will see still make the step look wrong. (1) At t=0.25 the four dot-matrix wires plainly go into the top of the Mini-B plug and come out under the board's edge. This is the centre of the view: exactly what Lee complained about, and the README calls it a "graze". (2) The cable changes through very unlike shapes during the turn: hanging straight at 0.20, a V-shaped hairpin at 0.25, an arch round the board's edge at 0.30, a loop across the board at 0.35, a flat loop at 0.40. Later it makes a pigtail curl beside the A end at 0.75. (3) At the stops at 0.70, 0.80 and 1.0, the cable doubles back across its own A end. check_caps never tests a wire against its own end parts, so the README's "nothing passes through anything in the A end's six beats" does not cover this. (4) In the last third (0.30-0.40), the button and 4-digit display bundles still pass through each other (56 contacts in the check). Also, the A end's final place, under the display's header end, still reads on screen as plugged into the display's header. The README's Step 42 paragraph is mostly true. It gives a wrong file name, understates the plug and board pass-through and leaves out the Nano Board contacts, places the board dips in the wrong third, and does not mention the hairpin, the pigtail or the doubled-back cable.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds up, but the reviewer overstates how far the README hides it.

What I confirmed:
- **The picture.** k42_1920_0250.png, crop (1520-1680, 560-720) enlarged 5x: the green, navy, maroon and teal wires go into the top of the right-angle Mini-B plug at about (1545-1560, 560-610). A teal speck pokes out of the plug's lower face at about (1580-1585, 648-655). The wires come out again under the board's edge at about (1600-1640, 660-700).
- **It happens over time, not in one frame.** A strip of 0.15 / 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.30 (crop 1480-1720, 520-760) shows the four wires in front of the plug at 0.20, inside it at 0.25 and behind the board at 0.30. So in the centre of the view the plug passes through the bundle somewhere between 0.20 and 0.30, which is up to 0.8 s of the 8 s motion (10 beats of 0.8 s). The same is visible, smaller, in k42_1000_0250.
- **The check agrees.** motion_check_42c_201.txt has GND/CLK/DIN/CS into NAUO282 (the plug) 4.23-4.34 mm at 0.24, into NAUO78 (the module) 2.19-3.07 mm at 0.24-0.26, VCC/CLK/CS into NANO 0.81-1.40 mm, and VCC into NAUO282 2.90 mm at 0.17.
- **The depth is real.** check_caps.py counts depth as the tube's surface reaching into the part (d + rad). The wires' radius in steps.json is 0.625 mm (1.25 mm thick), so at 4.3 mm the whole wire is about 3 mm inside the plug. That is a pass-through, not a graze.
- **The route settings are as the reviewer says.** Routes 151-154 have b_whole 16.76-16.99 mm, no b_from and no a_whole, and are 69-80 mm long. Route 150 (VCC) has b_whole 41.64 mm on 82.3 mm. wire_via keeps these bench routes for beats 1-3, so this is the skinning blend, not a route change.

Where the reviewer goes too far:
- The README does not hide the problem. It says "the dot matrix's wires graze the USB plug's end (up to 4.3 mm) and the board's edge (3 mm) for about a tenth of a second ... From this camera most of them can be seen". The depth, both parts and the fact that it can be seen are all there.
- What is wrong in the README:
  - "graze" undersells a 4.3 mm pass-through by a 1.25 mm wire.
  - "about a tenth of a second" is too short. The board contacts alone span 0.24-0.26 (at least 0.16 s), VCC is in the plug at 0.17, and the pictures place the crossing within 0.20-0.30.
  - The Nano Board contacts (0.8-1.4 mm) are not mentioned.
  - The buttons' wires dipping into the board are put "in the last third", but the check has them at 0.26-0.28.
- The reviewer's first fix is not supported. VCC already has a long b_whole (41.6 mm) and still goes into the plug (2.9 mm at 0.17), the module (3.07 mm at 0.24) and the Nano (1.40 mm). Raising b_whole on 151-154 is not shown to clear the plug.

Verdict: a real visible defect in the very thing Lee asked to have fixed, in the centre of the view and lasting a few tenths of a second. It is disclosed, but in words that make it sound imperceptible. Severity 2: minor, short-lived, small on screen (the plug is about 57 CSS px wide at 1920 and about 35 at 1000), and the README needs correcting before Lee relies on it.

- Name the Nano Board (0.8-1.4 mm).
- Say that VCC goes into the plug earlier (2.9 mm at 0.17).
- Say that the plug crosses the bundle over roughly 0.2-0.5 s, between 0.20 and 0.30 of the motion, in the middle of the view (it is not "a graze for a tenth of a second").

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds, though its mechanism needs a small correction and both of its proposed fixes have already been tried.

**What the pictures show.** I cropped k42_1920_0150 to _0500, and k42_760_0250 and k42_1000_0250.
- At t=0.20 the cable hangs smoothly from the plug to the table.
- At t=0.25 it forms a V under the plug at all three widths. The right arm ends in a rounded tip that reads as a cut end.
- At t=0.30 it is a tall arch round the board's edge.
- At t=0.35 and 0.40 it is a loop across the board's face, then one over the top.

**Route lengths.** steps.json confirms the cable's routes: 155 = 75.6, 177 = 108.4, 178 = 156.5, 179 = 292.8 and 180 = 339.6 mm. Step 42c's wire_via is [177..185], so routes change at the end of each beat.

**Why the V appears.** In the player, paced() gives the wires (2 + ease(0.5)) / 10 = 0.25 at t=0.25, so drawWires is half way from 178 to 179 (leg 2, f = 0.5).
- Both routes have tail_from = 40, so head = 40 and tail = max(116.5, 252.8) = 252.8 mm.
- For the shorter route 178, the tail samples start at 156.5 - 252.8 = -96 mm. sampled() clamps everything below 40 mm, so about 74 of the 160 samples sit on one point, A(40).
- The blend there is (A(40) + B(d)) / 2 for d from 40 to 177 mm. That is route 179's arch at half scale, pinned at the 40 mm point.

I ran a numpy copy of skinned() and the tail_from blend, using mixPose for the plug and Step 42's view_dir. Seen from that view, the shape at f = 0.5 doubles back: samples about 25 to 50 go up to a sharp tip and samples 50 to 95 come back down nearly on top of them. In 3D the two strokes are about 10 mm apart along the line of sight (worst turn 63 degrees within 6 mm), so it is not a true fold. On screen, though, it is exactly the hairpin in the pictures.

**Cause.** The cause is mainly the 137 mm length jump in beat 3, not only unlike shapes. The other module beats add 33, 48 and 47 mm, and their mid-beat frames (0.05, 0.15, 0.35) show no hairpin.

**Not disclosed.** README.txt's round-3 section mentions the 76 to 340 mm growth and says "the cable folded flat at the plug" was fixed. It does not mention this mid-beat hairpin. Nothing passes through anything, and it lasts only a fraction of one 0.8 s beat. But it is the kind of confusing wire motion Lee asked about in Step 42, so severity 2.

**The proposed fixes.** guide.py already records trying both:
